claims.text: CodePipeline's default execution mode is `SUPERSEDED`.
In CodePipeline's `SUPERSEDED` execution mode, a stage is locked to one execution at a time.
In `SUPERSEDED` mode, a newer execution can overtake an execution that is still waiting to enter a locked stage, dropping it before it starts.
In `SUPERSEDED` mode, a queued execution waiting behind a busy CodeBuild stage running `pulumi up` can be superseded and never run, silently skipping a deployment.
Setting CodePipeline execution mode to `QUEUED` makes waiting executions form a queue and each runs in turn.
The CodePipeline `QUEUED` execution mode requires a V2 pipeline (`pipelineType`).
The AWS CLI `create-pipeline` and `update-pipeline` commands can set `executionMode` and `pipelineType` for a pipeline.
The `aws.codepipeline.Pipeline` resource in the Pulumi AWS provider accepts `executionMode` and `pipelineType` inputs.
When two runs reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one of them, and the other's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
Azure Pipelines supports an exclusive lock check on an environment that can prevent concurrent deployment runs targeting that environment.
The exclusive lock check is added from the environment's 'Approvals and checks' tab in Azure DevOps.
In Azure Pipelines YAML, `lockBehavior` can be set on a stage to control how the exclusive lock is applied to queued runs.
The default value of `lockBehavior` in Azure Pipelines is `runLatest`.
With `lockBehavior: runLatest`, only the most recently queued run acquires the exclusive lock, and older runs waiting are passed over (cancelled) rather than eventually applied.
With `lockBehavior: sequential`, every queued stage runs against the lock in order, one at a time.
Pulumi Cloud serializes updates to a stack, one at a time in order.
The Azure DevOps provider in the Pulumi Registry has a `azuredevops.CheckExclusiveLock` resource for managing the exclusive lock check as code.
Link targets exist: /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ and /registry/packages/azuredevops/api-docs/checkexclusivelock/
When two runs of the same build configuration reach the same Pulumi stack at once, Pulumi Cloud grants the update lease to only one, and the other's `pulumi up` fails with an update conflict.
TeamCity's default is to let build configurations run concurrently against as many free agents as are available.
In TeamCity, the build configuration advanced option 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' defaults to 0 (unlimited).
The 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' option is located under the build configuration's General Settings in TeamCity.
With TeamCity's 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' set to 1, a second build is queued behind the first and runs only once the first finishes.
Pulumi Cloud has a per-stack lease that gives one-at-a-time update behavior.
There is a Pulumi docs page at /docs/iac/operations/troubleshooting/update-conflicts/ describing update conflicts.
In Azure Pipelines, adding an exclusive lock check to the environment targeted by a deployment job serializes Pulumi deployments.
In Azure Pipelines, the `lockBehavior: sequential` setting on a stage is used with an exclusive lock check so that deployments run sequentially.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/azure-devops/ has a section 'serialize-deployments-with-an-exclusive-lock'.
AWS CodePipeline's execution mode can be set to `QUEUED` so waiting executions run in turn.
AWS CodePipeline's default execution mode (SUPERSEDED) lets a newer execution supersede an older one that is still waiting to start.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/aws-code-services/ has a section 'serialize-pipeline-executions'.
In TeamCity, the build configuration setting 'Limit the number of simultaneously running builds' set to 1 prevents concurrent deployment builds.
The Pulumi docs page /docs/iac/operations/continuous-delivery/teamcity/ has a section 'limit-concurrent-builds'.
